title: Great Bear Hassock
summary: Great Bear Hassock is one of three Hassock entries grouped around Rockaway and East Rockaway Inlet. It is identified as a tract of meadow near East Rockaway Inlet.
address_label: East Rockaway Inlet, Queens/Nassau County, New York
map_geometry_source: Approximate general location based on Tooker identifying Great Bear Hassock as a meadow tract near East Rockaway Inlet; offset slightly for map visibility.
history_content: Great Bear Hassock is preserved as a named meadow tract in the inlet landscape. Because the source places it near East Rockaway Inlet without boundaries, the location shown here uses a modern inlet-area point.
translation_content:
The Hassock group is explained through Algonquian words for marshy land. Related language examples include Narragansett hassucki, meaning marsh land, and Delaware assisku, meaning miry or marshy. Early documents also used related forms such as Hassokie and Hassokey for marsh, meadow, or swamp places.

Why Place Names Matter

“Geographical names are more than just labels on maps; they are a cultural legacy. They can tell us about our history and the values of previous generations. They can reveal trends in exploration and land settlement, resource use and cultural development. They provide us with a sense of both place and time.”

— Ron Kelland, Place Names Matter (2012), Municipal Heritage Forum program, Place Names Matter description
land_loss_content: Great Bear Hassock points to the importance of meadow and inlet landscapes in Long Island placenames. Keeping it separate from nearby Hassock entries helps preserve the distinct local features Tooker recorded while making clear that the precise tract is not mapped here.
whereintheworld_content: The point shown is an approximate general marker near East Rockaway Inlet. It is offset slightly for map visibility and is not an exact historic boundary or meadow coordinate.
